Not all carotenoids demonstrate promising anticancer effects. Beta-carotene is a 
carotenoid found in many foods that are orange in color, including sweet potatoes, 
carrots, cantaloupe, squash, apricots, pumpkin, and mangos. In 1994, a cancer 
­prevention study known as the Alpha-Tocopherol (Vitamin E)/Beta-Carotene Cancer 
Prevention Study (ATBC) found that lung cancer rates of male smokers increased in 
those who received beta-carotene supplements.50 Thus smokers should be warned 
not to take beta-carotene supplements.
